chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Sarrad, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever cuts a new garment and recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-qadr' thirty-six times, and when he reaches 'Tanazzal al-mala'ikah', he takes some water and sprinkles it lightly on the garment, then prays two rak'ahs and supplicates to his Lord, saying in his supplication: 'All praise is for Allah who provided me with what I adorn myself with among people and cover my nakedness with and pray to my Lord in it,' and when he praises Allah, he will continue to have abundance in livelihood until that garment wears out.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward and ritual for cutting a new garment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith links the mundane act of tailoring with spiritual devotion, emphasizing the sanctification of daily provisions through specific dhikr. The ritual of sprinkling water while reciting Surah Al-Qadr thirty-three times transforms the garment into a vessel of barakah, promising sustained financial ease as long as the cloth remains in use. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating worship into everyday life, where gratitude for material blessings is directly tied to their continued flow.
